{{short description|American computer scientist}}

'''George H. Mealy''' (December 31, 1927 – June 21, 2010, in [[Scituate, Massachusetts|Scituate]], [[Massachusetts]])<ref>[http://www.tributes.com/show/George-Mealy-88865028 George H. Mealy obituary], tributes.com, retrieved 2015-04-20.</ref> was an American mathematician and computer scientist who invented the namesake [[Mealy machine]], a type of [[finite state transducer]]. He was also a pioneer of [[modular programming]],<ref>{{citation|title=Software Pioneers: Contributions to Software Engineering|year=2002|pages=480–493|contribution=JSP in Perspective|first=Michael|last=Jackson|editor1-first=Manfred|editor1-last=Broy|editor2-first=Ernst|editor2-last=Denert|publisher=Springer|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-59412-0_30|url=http://mcs.open.ac.uk/mj665/JSPPers1.pdf|access-date=2015-04-21|archive-date=2017-05-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516215344/http://mcs.open.ac.uk/mj665/JSPPers1.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=The Origins of JSP and JSD: a Personal Recollection|department=Anecdotes|first=Michael|last=Jackson|journal=IEEE Annals of the History of Computing|volume=22|issue=2|year=2000|pages=61–63|doi=10.1109/MAHC.2000.841138|editor-first=James E.|editor-last=Tomayko|url=http://users.mct.open.ac.uk/mj665/JSPDOrgn.pdf|access-date=2015-04-21|archive-date=2024-04-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240422173727/http://users.mct.open.ac.uk/mj665/JSPDOrgn.pdf|url-status=dead}}.</ref> one of the lead designers of the [[Information Processing Language|IPL-V]] programming language,<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Simon | first1 = Herbert A. | author1-link = Herbert A. Simon
 | last2 = Newell | first2 = Allen | author2-link = Allen Newell
 | date = January 1986
 | doi = 10.1109/MAHC.1986.10020
 | issue = 1
 | journal = IEEE Annals of the History of Computing
 | pages = 47–49
 | title = Information Processing Language V on the IBM 650
 | url = https://saltworks.stanford.edu/assets/cr262jy3502.pdf
 | volume = 8| s2cid = 18999471 }}.</ref> and an early advocate of [[General-purpose macro processor|macro processors]] in [[assembly language]] programming.<ref>{{citation|title=Macro memories, 1964–2013|journal=[[TUGboat]]|volume=35|year=2014|issue=1|pages=99–109|url=http://walden-family.com/texland/tb109walden-preprint.pdf|first=David|last=Walden}}.</ref>

Mealy went to [[Harvard University]], where he was active in [[radio]] as business manager for [[WHRB]].<ref>{{citation|title=WHRB Officers|date=February 17, 1951|newspaper=[[The Harvard Crimson]]|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1951/2/17/whrb-officers-pwhrb-yesterday-announced-the/}}.</ref> He graduated in 1951 with an A.B., and at that time began working for [[Bell Laboratories]].<ref>{{citation|title=Contributors to This Issue|journal=[[Bell System Technical Journal]]|volume=38|issue=2|year=1959|pages=606–610|doi=10.1002/j.1538-7305.1959.tb03904.x|doi-access=free}}.</ref> He later worked at the [[RAND Corporation]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mealy |first1=George |title=Letters to the editor: Boolean rings |journal=Communications of the ACM |date=May 1961 |volume=4 |issue=5 |doi=10.1145/366532.366590}}</ref> then [[IBM]]<ref>{{cite journal |title=Author Biographies |journal=IBM Systems Journal |date=1966 |volume=5 |issue=1 |page=52 |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?arnumber=5388469 |access-date=11 January 2024}}</ref> and taught at Harvard.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=143691}}</ref>

== Other contributions ==
In a 2024 article in ''[[Data & Knowledge Engineering]]'', researchers described Mealy's 1967 paper "Another Look at Data" as containing the first mention of the term "[[Ontology (information science)|ontology]]" in [[computer science]], quoting his statement: "Data are fragments of a theory of the real world, and data processing juggles representations of these fragments of theory{{nbsp}}... The issue is one of ontology, or the question of what exists."
